examples.en: The long journey of preparing for the Olympics has finally begun.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 전국 투어 대장정을 마치고 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: The singer came back after finishing a long nationwide tour.

examples.ko: 십 년간의 대장정 끝에 책이 완성됐어요.
examples.en: After a ten-year-long effort, the book was completed.
The players set out on the long road toward the championship.
This long journey was really long and hard.
We safely finished the long journey that was shooting the film.

explain: 실제 먼 길뿐 아니라 오래 걸리고 힘든 큰 일이나 프로젝트를 비유할 때 많이 써요. '대장정에 오르다/나서다', '대장정을 마치다'처럼 짝지어 쓰고, 가벼운 여행에는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀은 새 앨범 제작의 대장정에 올랐어요.
phrases.en: Our team set out on the long journey of making a new album.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 힘든 일을 시작할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for starting a big, difficult undertaking.
phrases.en_equiv: set out on a long journey

phrases.en: I graduated after finishing a three-year epic journey.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 걸린 일이 끝났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a long, demanding task is finished.

phrases.en: After a long journey, I achieved my dream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻의 쉬운 말로, 오래 걸린 과정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, similar phrase for a long process.

explain_en: Besides a literal long trek, it is often used figuratively for a big, long, demanding project. It pairs with '대장정에 오르다/나서다' and '대장정을 마치다', and it is not used for a light trip.

examples.en: The new business has finally gotten on track.

examples.ko: 공사가 본궤도에 오르려면 시간이 더 걸려요.
examples.en: It will take more time for construction to get properly on track.
The economy is slowly returning to its normal course.
The project has settled onto its track, so I feel relieved.
It will take time for the economy to get back on track.
I put the derailed schedule back on track.

explain: '본궤도에 오르다/들어서다'처럼 거의 정해진 모양으로 써요. 시작 단계를 지나 일이 안정적으로 잘 굴러간다는 뜻이에요. 비슷하게 '궤도에 오르다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: The new shop is finally on track.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 안정적으로 잘 굴러가기 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things start running smoothly.

phrases.en: The project has finally got on track.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오르다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 시작 단계를 지났다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '오르다', suggesting the start phase is over.
phrases.en_equiv: to move onto the main track

phrases.en: The business is on track, so I'm relieved.
phrases.nuance_ko: '본'을 뺀 모양이에요. 말할 때 더 짧게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form without '본', which is shorter in speech.

explain_en: It is used almost only in set forms like '본궤도에 오르다/들어서다'. It means a matter has passed the starting stage and is running steadily. People also say '궤도에 오르다' in a similar way.

examples.en: On the downhill road, the bike zooms along.
The wind is whistling hard, so it's really cold.
Cars whiz by on the highway.

examples.ko: 아이가 눈 위에서 씽씽 썰매를 타요.
examples.en: The child zips along on a sled over the snow.
I read a book on the speeding train.
A motorcycle whizzed past me.

explain: 무언가가 빠르게 달리거나 바람이 세게 불 때 쓰는 말이에요. '쌩쌩'과 느낌이 비슷해요. 속도가 시원스럽게 빠르다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: Cars whiz by on the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르게 옆을 스쳐 가는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for something rushing past you quickly.

phrases.en: I rode a bus speeding along the highway.
phrases.nuance_ko: '씽씽' 뒤에 '달리는'을 붙여 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can put '달리는' after it to describe a noun.

phrases.nuance_ko: '씽씽'과 거의 같지만 조금 더 센 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as '씽씽' but a bit stronger.

explain_en: It is used for something moving fast or wind blowing strongly. The feel is similar to '쌩쌩'. It carries a sense of brisk, refreshing speed.

examples.en: The front wheel of my bicycle went flat.
The front wheel was wobbling, so I went to the repair shop.
I replaced the motorcycle's front wheel with a new one.
The trick of riding with the front wheel up is difficult.
The car's front wheel fell into a puddle hole.
The front tire is badly worn.

explain: 앞쪽에 달린 바퀴이고 반대말은 '뒷바퀴'예요. 소리는 [압빠퀴]로 나니까 소리 나는 대로 쓰지 않도록 조심하세요. 자전거, 오토바이, 자동차 이야기에서 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I replaced both the front and rear wheels with new ones.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs the word with its opposite, rear wheel.

phrases.en: The front tire got a flat, so I walked here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자전거나 차 바퀴에 문제가 생겼을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when a bike or car tire has a problem.

phrases.en: I checked the car's front wheels.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자전거 말고 다른 탈것에 붙여서도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can attach other vehicles to the word, not only bicycles.

explain_en: It is the wheel at the front, and the opposite is '뒷바퀴'. It is pronounced [압빠퀴], so be careful not to spell it as it sounds. It often comes up when talking about bicycles, motorcycles and cars.

examples.en: On the weekend I went to the amusement park with my family.
There is a bike path in the riverside recreation area.
I bought cotton candy at the entrance of the recreation area.
That recreation park has pretty cherry blossoms in spring.
Old amusement parks had many small rides.
There are many restaurants near the recreation area, so it's convenient.

explain: 놀이기구가 있는 '놀이공원'이나 '놀이동산'보다 더 넓은 말이에요. 강가나 바닷가, 공원에 놀이기구와 식당이 있는 오래된 나들이 장소에 어울려요. 요즘은 '놀이공원'이라는 말이 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: We ate a packed lunch at the recreation park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유원지에서 한 일을 말할 때 '에서'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 에서 to say what you did at the park.

phrases.en: I met my friend at the entrance of the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속 장소를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when naming a meeting place.

phrases.en: I took a walk at the seaside recreation park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유원지가 어디에 있는지 앞에 붙여 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can put the location before the word to say where the park is.

explain_en: This is a broader word than 놀이공원 or 놀이동산. It suits older outing spots by rivers, seas or parks with rides and restaurants. These days 놀이공원 is the more common word.

examples.en: The team arrived safely in Beijing yesterday.
When the army entered the city, people cheered.

examples.ko: 대표팀은 내일 경기가 열리는 도시에 입성해요.
examples.en: The national team arrives tomorrow in the city hosting the match.

examples.ko: 새 감독이 오늘 팀에 입성할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The new coach is set to join the team today.

examples.ko: 서울에 입성하는 날 비가 많이 왔어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot on the day I arrived in Seoul.

examples.ko: 시골에서 올라온 청년이 대도시에 입성하고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The young man who came up from the countryside was stunned on arriving in the big city.

explain: 성이나 도시 안으로 들어서는 큰 장면에 어울리는 말이에요. 요즘은 뉴스에서 선수단이나 가수가 새 도시나 팀에 도착할 때 많이 써요. 행사장 안으로 들어갈 때는 '입장하다'를 써서 쓰임이 달라요.

phrases.en: The team is about to enter the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 어떤 곳에 들어갈 때 쓰는 짝말로 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for being about to enter a place, common in news.

phrases.en: As soon as he entered the city, he went to his lodging.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어선 바로 뒤에 다른 일이 이어질 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form for something that happens right after entering.

phrases.en: The news spread that the king had entered the castle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 들어왔다는 소식을 전할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when passing on news that someone has made an entrance.

explain_en: It fits a big scene of entering a walled city or capital. In today's news it's used when a team or singer arrives in a new city or joins a new team. For going into an event venue, use 입장하다 instead.
